languageTrainerCard.title: Language trainer
languageTrainerCard.description: The language trainer is a practice area in the studio for everyone following the course in a foreign language. It holds vocabulary cards for technical terms and a grammar exercise, each built from the workspace sources. While it is on, every reader is assessed once and chat answers as well as exercises are pitched at that level.
languageTrainerCard.active: Active. Owners and tutors decide in the workspace settings whether their course offers the language trainer. They need suitable sources on the grammar of the course language for it.
languageTrainerCard.disabled: Off. The language trainer appears nowhere. Choices already made stay stored and apply again as soon as you switch this on.

ocrCard.title: OCR for scans & image pages
ocrCard.active: Active - image/scan-heavy pages are captured via OCR during indexing (slower, costs one vision call per page).
ocrCard.disabled: Disabled - OCR is skipped system-wide. Indexing is faster and cheaper, but pure scan/image pages stay empty for search.
ocrCard.hint: Applies to all workspaces and new indexing. Existing documents are only affected after re-indexing.

languageDiagnosisCard.title: Language diagnosis prompt
languageDiagnosisCard.description: Controls how the AI asks, judges and grades in the diagnosis chat. Applies to every workspace. German only for now.
languageDiagnosisCard.hint: Controls the flow, the question style and the output format of the test. Four placeholders in the text are filled in: '{language}' with the language of the test, '{grading}' with the grading rules below, '{levels}' with the descriptions from the Levels A1 to C2 card and '{examples}' with the example sentences from there. A placeholder you delete is appended at the end, so the AI never loses it.

diagnosisPlanCard.title: Question plan
diagnosisPlanCard.description: Decides which questions the placement test asks. Each row is one question with one of two task types. Choice means clicking and needs answer options with at least one marked correct. Free text means typing and needs only the question text. The solution on a free text is optional and decides who marks it: with a solution the code checks the answer word for word, without one the AI judges it at the end. Anything that belongs before the question, a short reading text or an everyday situation, simply goes into the question text. The order is the order in the test and runs from easy to hard. Either you write everything yourself, or you let the AI write it once and read it through. The test itself then runs without a single AI call. The AI assigns the level A1 to C2 at the end from the answers, not per question.
diagnosisPlanCard.languageHint: The test is in German, so questions and options are too.
diagnosisPlanCard.freeTextHint: At least 2 free-text questions without a solution are required. Only those does the AI judge itself, and only they give the level a real writing sample.
diagnosisPlanCard.judgedCount: Free text without a solution, judged by the AI: {count} of at least {min}.
diagnosisPlanCard.optionsHint: Mark exactly one correct. Several are allowed if the question says so.
diagnosisPlanCard.answersHint: Leave it empty if the AI should judge the answer. If you enter a solution, the code checks the typed answer and this question needs no AI at all. One solution per line, every line counts as correct. Capitalisation and a final punctuation mark are ignored, accents and umlauts are not. Short solutions give the learner a one-line box, whole sentences the big one.
diagnosisPlanCard.gradedByCodeHint: Checked without AI. The typed answer has to match one of the solutions.
diagnosisPlanCard.gradedByAiHint: The AI judges this answer at the end, using the grading rules and the level examples from the AI behaviour tab. This row counts towards the required writing samples.
diagnosisPlanCard.generate: Let the AI write the questions
diagnosisPlanCard.generatingHint: This takes about a minute. The AI writes a complete set of questions, and you can change every one of them afterwards.
diagnosisPlanCard.generateFailed: The AI could not write a set of questions. Please try again.
diagnosisPlanCard.generateWarningResult: You get {count} new questions with a fixed sequence of task types, from easy to hard. The number and the task types follow that sequence, not your current list.

adaptiveBehaviorCard.title: Adaptive answer behaviour
adaptiveBehaviorCard.description: Controls how the AI answers learners in the normal chat, depending on their level. Only takes effect when a level is stored.
adaptiveBehaviorCard.hint: Controls tone and wording. Three placeholders in the text are filled in, always for the learner's own level: '{level}' with the level itself, '{description}' with its description from the Levels A1 to C2 card and '{example}' with the example sentences from there. Delete a placeholder and that piece is simply missing.

diagnosisGradingCard.title: Grading rules
diagnosisGradingCard.description: Defines the procedure: what the AI looks at when placing a learner.
diagnosisGradingCard.hint: This text has no placeholders of its own. It is inserted into the language diagnosis prompt above at '{grading}'. What defines a level is not here, it lives in the Levels A1 to C2 card.

diagnosisLevelsCard.title: Levels A1 to C2
diagnosisLevelsCard.description: What defines a level. The AI places learners by it in the test and writes by it in the chat.
diagnosisLevelsCard.hint: Use the same situation for every level, so the AI sees one statement rising through the levels.
diagnosisLevelsCard.descriptionLabel: How someone writes at this level

scheduleRetentionCard.hint: Past entries (done or not) are automatically deleted daily after this many days. Leave empty for 'never delete' (default). Future entries are always kept.

contextBudgetCard.title: AI tutor context budget
contextBudgetCard.hint: How much source text (in characters) the AI tutor sends to the model per question. The default 60000 is safe for small models (32k). If a selected source fits entirely within the budget, it is sent whole for overview questions instead of a retrieved sample. Raise only if you run exclusively large-context models.

toolContextBudgetCard.title: Tools context budget
toolContextBudgetCard.hint: How much source text (in characters) the learning tools (mind map, data table, quiz, flashcards, glossary, cloze, cards) send to the model. Separate from the chat budget because a tool processes a whole document in one call. The value is divided by the number of selected sources. The default 250000 is safe for mid-tier models. Raise it (e.g. 450000 or 900000) only when running a large-context model.

summaryBatchCard.title: Summary – batch size
summaryBatchCard.hint: How much text (in characters) is sent to the model per summary call during upload. Larger = fewer calls (eases the provider's rate limit), but each partial summary gets coarser. Default 360000 (~72 pages) is a good balance.

sourceMaxPagesCard.title: Max. pages per source
sourceMaxPagesCard.hint: Maximum number of pages an uploaded document (PDF/DOCX/PPTX) may have. Larger ones are rejected — please upload long scripts chapter by chapter. Default 100: keeps each source small enough for a complete overview. Media (mp3/mp4) is not affected.

auth.heading: 2. Authentication and user account
auth.intro: Access to the platform is provided via a directory service. The following data is stored in our database:
auth.outro:
Passwords are not stored on this platform; authentication is handled exclusively against the directory service.
Legal basis: Art. 6 (1) (e) GDPR (performance of a task carried out in the public interest).
Retention period: until the user account is deleted.

cookies.heading: 3. Cookies and local storage
cookies.intro: This platform uses only technically necessary cookies and storage mechanisms:
cookies.sessionBody: An HttpOnly cookie used for authentication (valid for 24 hours). Without this cookie, login is not possible.
cookies.storageBody: Temporary storage of filter settings in the browser (automatically cleared when the tab is closed).
cookies.outro: No tracking, analytics or marketing cookies are used. Cookie data is not shared with third parties.

jobs.heading: 4. Processing of user uploads and job data
jobs.intro: When you use the platform, uploaded files (e.g. videos, PDFs, presentations, audio files) and the results derived from them (e.g. transcripts, summaries) are stored in your workspace. For each processing job, the following metadata is also stored:
jobs.retention: Uploaded files and the results derived from them remain stored in your workspace until you or a workspace administrator deletes them. Job metadata for individual processing jobs is automatically removed after no more than 7 days.

thirdParty.heading: 5. Third parties and external AI services
thirdParty.intro: To provide the AI features, content is transmitted to external services:
thirdParty.kisskiBody: Language models and transcription services. Texts and audio content are processed in this context. KISSKI is a service of Gesellschaft für wissenschaftliche Datenverarbeitung mbH Göttingen (GWDG) and is subject to German data protection law. Processing takes place under a data processing agreement pursuant to Art. 28 GDPR.
thirdParty.outro: Only the content required for the respective function is transmitted. The third-party providers do not retain the data beyond the duration of processing.

logs.heading: 6. Server log files
logs.intro: When this website is accessed, the web server automatically records information in so-called server log files. This includes:
logs.item1: IP address of the requesting device
logs.retention: This data is automatically deleted after no more than 7 days.

ssl.heading: 7. SSL/TLS encryption
ssl.body: The platform uses SSL/TLS encryption to securely transmit data. You can recognise an encrypted connection by the browser address bar starting with "https://".

legalBasis.heading: 8. Legal basis
legalBasis.body: Processing is based on Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (legitimate interest) for server logs, and on Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR (performance of a contract) for user data and job processing within the scope of platform usage.

rights.heading: 9. Your rights as a data subject
rights.intro: You have the following rights vis-à-vis the data controller regarding personal data concerning you:
rights.item4: Right to restriction of processing (Art. 18 GDPR)
rights.item6: Right to object to processing (Art. 21 GDPR)
rights.contact: To exercise these rights, please contact:

complaint.heading: 10. Right to lodge a complaint
complaint.body: You have the right to lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority. The competent authority is the Unabhängiges Landeszentrum für Datenschutz Schleswig-Holstein (ULD Kiel) (Independent State Data Protection Centre of Schleswig-Holstein).

settings.title: Settings
settings.sectionPersonalDescription: Applies to you only. Others in the workspace do not see any of this.
settings.sectionWorkspaceDescription: Applies to everyone in the workspace. Only workspace admins can change it.
settings.studioDescription: Show the studio panel with mind maps, notes and tools.
settings.languageTrainingPersonalDescription: Shows the language trainer for you, with vocabulary cards and grammar exercise. Switching it on assesses your language level once if you do not have one yet. Applies to you only and only in this workspace.
settings.languageTrainingDescription: Releases the language trainer in this workspace, with vocabulary cards and grammar exercise. Everyone then decides in their own settings whether to use it. Every exercise is built from the sources of this workspace. That needs suitable sources on the grammar of the course language, otherwise the exercises are useless. Only release this when you know which sources are here.
settings.translationModeDescription: Translates subtitles of audio/video sources into the target language chosen below. The source language is detected automatically. Students can switch between original and translation in the transcript panel. Translation runs as a background job and can take a few minutes.
settings.translationModeAutoHint: Translation starts automatically once a source is indexed.
settings.translationModeManualHint: Translation only on click in the transcript panel (default).
settings.transcriptTargetLangDescription: Which language transcripts are translated into. The source language is detected automatically. Transcripts are always translated into exactly one language.
settings.transcriptDefaultLangDescription: Which track is preselected when an audio/video source is opened. Students can switch any time in the transcript panel.
settings.popupTranslateLangDescription: Which language selected text is translated into when you tap Translate in the selection bar.
